subject: Scoped retention request and SIG evidence: ClearBay Health (tenant-specific 7y ask)
messages:
From: Sarah Mitchell <sarah.mitchell@clearbayhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearbayhealth.com
Date: 2028-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question: tenant-scoped log retention for regulatory audits (SIG follow-up)

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for walking through the SIG with our security team last week. A couple of items bubbled up on our side around retention: ClearBay has a regulatory requirement to retain transaction identifiers tied to billing and claims activities for up to 7 years for a small subset of customers (state-level audits).

Specifically we want to confirm whether Redwood can:
  - support a per-tenant (customer-scoped) retention exception so that those transaction identifiers are retained for 7 years while keeping all other request bodies at your standard TTL;
  - provide an evidentiary export for audits (CSV of retained identifiers + access logs showing who exported it);
  - isolate the retained items (separate S3 prefix or bucket) and use a dedicated KMS key or similar control.

Can you point me to the evidence that maps how request/response logs are stored today (paths, TTLs, redaction patterns), and confirm whether Redwood would treat raw PHI differently from indexed transaction IDs? We attached the latest SIG questions (Q4.2 / Q6.1 notes) — please flag anything we missed.

Appreciate a short mutual action plan (next steps, owners, rough timeline) so procurement can align on the addendum we may need.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Mitchell
Security & Compliance Lead, ClearBay Health
sarah.mitchell@clearbayhealth.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: tenant-scoped log retention for regulatory audits (SIG follow-up)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. Looping Neha (security) and Karthik (legal/compliance) so we can propose an operational path.

High level answer up front: Redwood supports customer-scoped retention exceptions but we treat raw PHI and indexed identifiers differently by default. We can scope an exception for non-PII identifiers and provide an export path for audit purposes, but we need to agree on controls and an amendment that defines the exact attributes, export cadence, and cost impact.

A few clarifying questions that will help us scope:
  1) Which specific fields do you need retained for 7 years? (transaction_id, claim_id, billing_id — please list exact attribute names)
  2) Is the retention demand limited to production tenant(s) only?
  3) Do you require separation of storage (dedicated prefix/bucket) and a unique KMS key, or is RBAC/audit-only access sufficient?

Proposed interim approach (we can refine after answers):
  - Tiered retention: indexed identifiers (transaction_id, claim_id) stored in a tenant-tagged export table for up to 7 years; raw request/response bodies (potentially containing PHI) kept to standard 30 days unless you request a separate retention addendum and provide lawful basis;
  - Access & export: exports generated through a controlled admin workflow with export logs and signed attestation;
  - Controls: dedicated S3 prefix + per-tenant KMS key (optional), strict IAM roles for export, and quarterly access reviews.

I've attached a draft SIG response with the current retention map and a sample CSV extract (log-retention-sample.csv). If that direction looks acceptable, Neha/Karthik and I will produce a short retention amendment and cost estimate.

Next steps (suggested):
  - Sarah: confirm exact attributes and tenants in scope by EOD Wed
  - Redwood: provide amendment draft, implementation plan, and preliminary cost estimate within 3 business days of scope confirmation

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Question: tenant-scoped log retention for regulatory audits (SIG follow-up)

Evelyn — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft files. To be concrete:
  - Attributes: claim_id, transaction_id, provider_npi (hashed), and settlement_reference.
  - Tenants: two production tenants (CBH-NY and CBH-CA) only.
  - Separation: we prefer a separate S3 prefix + customer-specific KMS key; procurement will need the cost delta before we sign an addendum.

We cannot accept raw request bodies being stored beyond 30 days. The retained fields above are not PHI as stored by our system (provider_npi will be hashed by us), but regulators still want the identifiers for traceability. We also need a documented export workflow (who can request, approval process, export retention) and proof that exports are recorded in access logs for audits.

If you can provide the amendment + cost estimate and the implementation timeline, procurement will prepare a DocuSign amendment.

Thanks,
Sarah

Evelyn / Karthik — quick feasibility notes from security/infra:

  - Implementation: achievable. We'll tag the two tenants and route the identified attributes into a per-tenant retention bucket (separate prefix) at write-time. We can optionally use S3 Object Lock in GOVERNANCE mode for the 7-year window; recommend using a dedicated KMS key with strict key policy limiting decryption to a small set of ops accounts.
  - PHI: we must enforce that raw request bodies are redacted at ingest (30-day TTL). Anything that may contain free-text PHI cannot be moved into the long-lived retention store. That matches your guidance.
  - Export workflow: we can create an internal export tool that requires: (1) requestor identity, (2) two approvers (ops + security), (3) signed export log saved to the tenant's audit prefix. Exports will be hashed and stored for 90 days.
  - Forensics & audit evidence: we can provide a CSV sample (attached) and a CloudTrail-style access log slice for the export window.
  - Cost: preliminary infra delta ~USD 1,800 - 2,400 / month (object lock + KMS + extra storage); will refine after we estimate volume.

I will produce an implementation checklist and the exact IAM/KMS bindings for Karthik to include in the addendum.

—Neha

Hi Sarah — thanks for the confirmation and scope. To summarize and confirm next steps so procurement can move to DocuSign:

What Redwood will provide:
  - Per-tenant retention: indexed fields (claim_id, transaction_id, provider_npi-hash, settlement_reference) placed into a tenant-tagged retention bucket and retained for up to 7 years; raw request/response bodies will continue to be redacted/TTL'd at 30 days.
  - Storage & controls: separate S3 prefix per tenant, optional S3 Object Lock (Governance), dedicated per-tenant KMS key, and tenant-scoped access policies.
  - Export & evidence: controlled export workflow requiring dual approver sign-off; exports recorded in export logs saved to tenant audit prefix. We'll provide a sample export (log-retention-sample.csv) and an access-log sample for auditors.
  - Cost estimate: preliminary USD 2,100 / month (subject to volume) — final number in the addendum.

Action items and timeline:
  - Redwood (Neha): final implementation checklist and IAM/KMS bindings — 1 business day
  - Redwood (Karthik): retention addendum draft + export workflow language — 2 business days
  - Redwood (Evelyn): final cost estimate and consolidated scope to ClearBay — 3 business days after the above
  - ClearBay: confirm the two tenant IDs and sign the addendum in DocuSign once received

Attachments: retention-amendment-draft.docx; log-retention-sample.csv

If that aligns, let me know and we'll kick off work with infra.

Best,
